Taken to be the Legacy edition since it ran on DXMT. Minor issues not described. AsynchronousAI commented the same day that in their experience it plays perfectly, with no minor issues. Anphamthanh (highball-db#1404, 2026-11-23), Apple M4 Pro, macOS 27.0.1, Highball 0.10.26, engine x64-crossover26.3-r35, DXMT, rated 4 of 5: the Steam copy in story mode with -nobattleye, on a 64 GB Mac mini at 2560x1440, about 15 minutes in when filed with the game still running, frame rate not measured. On the Wine 11 engine r31 the game died at 'Entering Story Mode' twice: Steam's client called D3DKMTSetProcessSchedulingPriorityClass, which that engine's GDI32 lacks, its main loop stalled, it ended on 'fatal stalled cross-thread pipe', and the overlay and GTA5.exe went down within a second (highball#699). On r35, which 0.10.26 doesn't ship and the player installed with highball engine install from the repository's spike/engines manifest, story mode loads and plays. The Steam overlay was off for the game as a precaution, and settings.xml set to borderless at 2560x1440 with VSync off and PauseOnFocusLoss 0, since the first start came up as an 800x600 window holding the mouse. Pressing Play in Steam's own window skips Highball's engine offer, and in an environment the steam recipe made on the Wine 10 engine, Steam's first run step then ran the Rockstar launcher's installer there, which hung after 'RockstarService.exe install'. Moving the environment to Wine 11 and applying the rockstar recipe installed it in 18 seconds. Killing GTA5.exe from outside takes Steam down with the same pipe assert, so stop it from the game or with Highball's Stop. siddhant-dev (highball-db#1428, 2026-11-24), Apple M3 Pro, macOS 26.7.3, Highball 0.10.26, engine x64-crossover26.3-r31, DXMT by the report (the environment's mode is D3DMetal), rated 5 of 5 after 82 minutes: with the game's recipe and the steam and controller-sdl recipes, no Steam id. Taken to be the Legacy edition since it ran on DXMT. A DualSense was identified as an Xbox controller.
notes:
Story mode plays. Needs engine x64-crossover26.3-r5 or later and the DXMT renderer. Launch it from Steam: Steam starts the Rockstar Games Launcher, which signs in and hands off to the game. The row passes -nobattleye on the Steam command line, the story-mode path: without it a fresh launcher profile starts GTA5_BE.exe and BattlEye's installer asks for its kernel driver, which cannot run under Wine (seen on an M4, 2026-10-03). Checked again 2026-10-03 on an M4, macOS 27.0, engine x64-crossover26.3-r16 (the Wine 11 engine with the fixed DXMT), DXMT: the launcher signed in through the Steam entitlement and the game reached its display calibration screen five minutes after Play, nothing played past it that run.

Both of the things that used to stop this game are fixed. The launcher's sign-in window is a Chromium surface whose GPU process draws into another process's window, which rendered nothing until engine patch 0007 (cross-process child swapchains) plus DXMT_ALLOW_CROSS_PROCESS_SWAPCHAIN=1, both of which the rockstar recipe applies. And the sign-in itself was refused for reasons that looked like a network or account problem but were the Mac's clock: with the time zone set automatically, it signs in.

GTA Online cannot work. BattlEye ships with the game (a BattlEye directory and GTA5_BE.exe) and is kernel-level anti-cheat, so online is out under Wine on any tool. Story mode is the whole claim here.

Community reports of about 120 fps on an M1 Pro were measured on CrossOver's own tree, often with frame generation on. Our range overlaps at the top but the low end is 60, and the open world has not been measured at all, so treat the community figure as an upper bound rather than an expectation.

A player report on 2026-09-24 rates it perfect after 36 minutes on an M1 with macOS 27.0, on the Wine 10 engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r5 rather than the Wine 11 one this entry says the launcher needs. That has not been checked here. One possible reason is a launcher that was already signed in, since the Wine 10 engine's problem was drawing the sign-in window, but that is a guess. Re-checked on 2026-10-05 on an M4 with the Wine 11 engine r15 and -nobattleye: launcher passed, the game opens on its first-run display calibration screen. On a base M1, udance4ever measured about 25 fps in the benchmark with settings.xml set to full screen at RefreshRate 30, and about 50 fps with RefreshRate 0 and Windowed 2, borderless (highball-db#72, 2026-10-09).

The Epic copy starts through the Rockstar launcher since Highball 0.10.15, which recognizes it as GTA V and starts it the way the launcher needs for an Epic license. Two players play it that way, one with the game's benchmark at 51 to 62 fps at 1080p on a base M1 (highball-db#415, highball#309). The other, on an M4, sees the frame rate swing up and down (highball-db#463).

Two things a player on an M1 MacBook Air found. A graphics change that restarts the renderer in game (Texture Quality, or Screen Type set to Fullscreen) leaves only the top-left quarter of the picture drawn until the game restarts, so change those settings with the game closed or restart it after. And the first load into story mode can stall for many minutes while the game window is not in front, because the game pauses itself without focus, so keep it in front or turn Pause Game On Focus Loss off. A DualSense or other PlayStation controller does not work in the game's menus, while an Xbox controller or a pad in XInput mode does (highball-db#72, #415). The M4 player's frame rate swings show in the Metal HUD's graph while play feels smooth at 50 to 60 fps in 1080p borderless. Exclusive fullscreen did not capture the mouse for them, and vehicle smoke showed purple lines on Very High that went away on High (highball-db#463). A player on an M2 Max sometimes sees the lighting turn far too bright, which a restart of the game fixes (highball-db#452). A player on an M3 Max with the Wine 11 engine r27 drove around for 46 minutes and saw weird texture artifacts, not described further (highball-db#622). The Epic copy was rated perfect on an M5 Pro with the Wine 11 engine and DXMT from a short session (highball-db#666). On an M1 Pro the Epic copy played 86 minutes, with frame drops when cutscenes or new areas load, cutscene audio sometimes running ahead of the video, and odd mouse movement at first (highball-db#671). Two more reports on the Wine 11 engine r31 with DXMT: the Epic copy played over 261 minutes on an M5, rated playable (highball-db#1265), and one perfect over 56 minutes on an M5 Pro (highball-db#1273). Rated playable with minor issues not described on an M3 with DXMT on the Wine 11 engine r31 over 8 minutes, started as PlayGTAV with -nobattleye (highball-db#1304). An M5 rated it playable with minor issues not described in a 1 minute session with DXMT on the Wine 11 engine r31 (highball-db#1327). An M4 Pro rated it perfect in an 8 minute session with DXMT on the Wine 11 engine r31 (highball-db#1343). An M3 Max rated it playable with minor issues not described over 133 minutes with DXMT on the Wine 11 engine r31 (highball-db#1357). On the Wine 11 engine r31 Steam's client can stall and take the game down at 'Entering Story Mode' (highball#699), which the Wine 11 engines from r32 fix (Highball 0.10.28). An M4 Pro played story mode on r35 (highball-db#1404).

anticheat.note: anti-cheat present; Linux/Proton support does not extend to macOS — userspace path works for some titles

requiresLauncher.name: Rockstar Games Launcher
requiresLauncher.note: Required. Steam starts it and it hands off to the game after sign-in. It installs and signs in on the Wine 11 engine (x64-crossover26.3-r15 or later) through the rockstar recipe, which Play applies and which offers that engine. The Wine 10 engine cannot draw its sign-in window, which is why the recipe moves the environment. The launcher last passed on an M4 with macOS 27.0 on 2026-10-05.

verified.fps: first-run display calibration reached, not played this run
verified.how: Steam copy through Highball on an M4 on 2026-10-05, DXMT, the Wine 11 engine r15, -nobattleye: launcher passed, the game opens on its first-run Display Calibration screen at 200 s.

knownIssues.symptom: The Rockstar launcher shows a blank or black sign-in window and the game never starts.
knownIssues.cause: the sign-in is a Chromium surface drawn by a separate GPU process into the browser process's window. Wine returned nothing for it until engine patch 0007.
knownIssues.fix: use engine x64-crossover26.3-r5 or later with the DXMT renderer (the recipe asks for r15, where the launcher installer works too), and apply the rockstar recipe, which sets DXMT_ALLOW_CROSS_PROCESS_SWAPCHAIN=1.

knownIssues.symptom: Sign in fails with 'Sorry, we are unable to handle your request at this time' (error 1.000.7).
knownIssues.cause: the Mac's clock being wrong, not the network or the account. Rockstar rejects the request. A second cause, confirmed 2026-10-24 by a player in Turkey (highball#477, M1 Max, macOS 27.0.1, Wine 11 r27): Wine names the Windows time zone by taking the first one in its list with the Mac's offset, so a Mac set to Europe/Istanbul reports Arab Standard Time (Riyadh) and Rockstar refuses the sign in, while the website works in a Mac browser.
knownIssues.fix: System Settings, General, Date & Time, with the time zone set automatically using your location. For the Turkey case, with the environment stopped, delete the seven UTC+3 zones listed before Turkey Standard Time (Arab, Arabic, Belarus, E. Africa, Jordan, Russian, Syria) under HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Time Zones in the environment's registry, which makes Wine report Turkey Standard Time. An engine update brings them back, so redo it after one. A fix in the engine is planned.

knownIssues.symptom: The BattlEye Launcher window asks to install BattlEye (Install / Cancel) and the game never starts (seen on an M4, Wine 11 engine r16, 2026-10-03)
knownIssues.cause: a fresh Rockstar launcher profile starts the game through GTA5_BE.exe, BattlEye's wrapper, and BattlEye's kernel driver cannot run under Wine
knownIssues.fix: start the game with -nobattleye, which Highball's Play passes for this game (from the next version after 0.10.4). By hand, put -nobattleye in Steam's launch options for the game, or turn BattlEye off for GTA V in the Rockstar launcher's settings. Story mode only either way

knownIssues.cause: BattlEye, a kernel-level anti-cheat, which cannot run under Wine.

knownIssues.symptom: A DualSense or other PlayStation controller does not work in the game, while it works in other games in the same environment (reported on an M1, highball-db#72, highball-db#415)
knownIssues.cause: not investigated. The game reads controllers through XInput and DirectInput. The player traced it to the DirectInput side, since an 8BitDo pad in XInput mode works (highball-db#415), and the only HID error in the first log names an Apple device (vendor 004c), not the DualSense
knownIssues.fix: use an Xbox controller or a pad in XInput mode. For the Steam copy, starting the game from Steam with Steam Input on also works, with the game added to Steam as a non-Steam game and -nobattleye in its launch options (highball-db#72, 2026-10-07)

knownIssues.symptom: The game starts at 800x600 in a window with low settings, or goes back to it after you set a resolution
knownIssues.cause: GTA V doesn't know the Apple GPU that DXMT presents, so on its first start it picks its lowest preset. It also resets to that preset whenever the graphics card it sees changes, for example with a settings.xml copied from Whisky or CrossOver, where D3DMetal presents an AMD card (udance4ever, highball-db#72).
knownIssues.fix: Set the resolution and quality once in the game's Graphics settings, they stay from then on. Don't copy settings.xml from another tool, or set the resolution again after doing it. Presenting an AMD card through DXMT_CONFIG made it worse in a test: the resolution list then held only the window size.

knownIssues.symptom: After a graphics change that restarts the renderer in game (Texture Quality, or Screen Type set to Fullscreen), only the top-left quarter of the picture shows, Retina on or off
knownIssues.cause: not investigated. Reported by a player on Discord on an M1 MacBook Air (2026-10-11)
knownIssues.fix: restart the game, which then draws correctly with the same settings, or change those settings with the game closed in Documents/Rockstar Games/GTA V/settings.xml

knownIssues.symptom: The first load into story mode stalls for many minutes (about 18 in one report) while the game window is not in front
knownIssues.cause: the game pauses itself while it does not have focus (Pause Game On Focus Loss, PauseOnFocusLoss in settings.xml). Reported by a player on Discord on an M1 MacBook Air (2026-10-11)
knownIssues.fix: keep the game in front during the load, or turn Pause Game On Focus Loss off

knownIssues.symptom: The lighting turns far too bright during play (M2 Max, highball-db#452)
knownIssues.fix: turn off the Steam overlay in game (Steam, Settings, In Game), which stopped it for the reporter. Setting Post FX to High in the game's graphics settings also helped (highball-db#452, 2026-10-19)

knownIssues.symptom: Weird texture artifacts (M3 Max, macOS 26.5.2, DXMT, Wine 11 engine r27, highball-db#622)
knownIssues.cause: not measured, and not described further in the report

knownIssues.symptom: The Rockstar launcher's sign-in window never appears after the launcher was used in another environment ('Timed out waiting for browser window' in socialclub_launcher.log, reported on an M4, macOS 27.0.1, highball#430)
knownIssues.cause: the launcher keeps its browser profile in Documents/Rockstar Games/Social Club/Launcher/Renderer, and every environment's Documents is the Mac's own Documents unless Keep game files inside this environment is on, so environments share that profile and one launcher could not read what another wrote. Found by Byron-aire
knownIssues.fix: with the launcher closed, rename that Renderer folder (the reporter added .bak) and press Play again, giving the sign-in window a minute or two to rebuild. Keep game files inside this environment keeps each environment's profile apart. The very first launch also updates the launcher and installs Social Club and can time out on that alone, so a second try often works

knownIssues.symptom: Shift+Tab freezes the game, then it crashes (reported on an M3 Pro, Wine 11 r27, DXMT, highball-db#697)
knownIssues.cause: Shift+Tab opens Steam's overlay over the game; not diagnosed further
knownIssues.fix: don't press Shift+Tab. Untested: turn off the Steam Overlay for this game in Steam (the game's Properties, General)

knownIssues.symptom: The Epic copy's first run needed the Rockstar Games Launcher started on its own first, to activate the Epic licence (M5, Wine 11 r29, DXMT). Until then the launcher can show Buy Now for GTA V although it is in the Epic library (M5, Wine 11 r31, highball-db#1265)
knownIssues.fix: connect Epic in Highball, install the Rockstar Games Launcher in the game's environment, start it by itself once, then Play (highball-db#1039, credit RicardoJardines, and highball-db#1265)

knownIssues.symptom: Short freezes when new parts of the world stream in, on DXVK and on DXMT (M5 MacBook Air 24 GB, macOS 26.7.1, Wine 11 r27, highball#419)
knownIssues.cause: not diagnosed. Most likely shaders compiled for Metal the first time an effect or area shows up. Whether it eases on a second pass through the same area was asked and not answered
knownIssues.fix: none confirmed. On DXVK, turning on DXVK async shader compilation in the environment's Graphics settings trades the freeze for brief pop in (untested for this game)

knownIssues.symptom: On the Wine 11 engine r31 the game dies at 'Entering Story Mode': Steam's client stalls ('fatal stalled cross-thread pipe') and the overlay and GTA5.exe crash with it (M4 Pro, highball-db#1404)
knownIssues.cause: Steam's client calls D3DKMTSetProcessSchedulingPriorityClass, which GDI32 lacks on that engine, the cause of highball#699
knownIssues.fix: the Wine 11 engine r32 or later (Highball 0.10.28 or later), picked under Advanced, Engine in the environment's settings. The reporter played on r35
